our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion makes US government AI deployment the relevant scope.
I read 'everywhere' as widespread routine deployment across government services, not literal deployment in every office.
I read 'unreliable' as producing material errors in the tasks for which the deployed systems are used.
I read 'most people will ignore' as more than half of exposed users failing to heed the warnings when using the systems.
'Soon' expresses urgency but supplies no defensible calendar deadline. I do not assign one.
Warning messages and users ignoring them are predicted features, not antecedents that make this a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Deployment records establish widespread routine government use of systems with material reliability problems and warnings, and representative behavioral evidence establishes that more than half of exposed users disregard those warnings.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence covering the same deployment population establishes that a central predicted feature is false, such as a representative majority consistently heeding warnings. With no fixed deadline, limited adoption at an interim date alone cannot establish failure.
